statement: A New York Times investigation reports $5.6 billion of advanced AI technology, including over $3 billion of Nvidia Blackwell-based AI servers, was allegedly routed to China between April 2024 and February 2026 through Inspur's US subsidiary Aivres.
why: Documented leakage of restricted accelerators to a blacklisted network is the kind of finding that triggers tighter export rules, which directly changes how much of the market a US merchant-GPU vendor can legally serve.

impact.mechanism: Evidence that current-generation Blackwell systems reached restricted Chinese buyers raises the odds of tighter licensing, subsidiary-level enforcement and lost addressable China revenue for merchant-GPU vendors.

evidence.source: freepressjournal.in (New York Times investigation, via IANS)
evidence.excerpt: in advanced AI technology allegedly sent to China between April 2024 and February 2026, moved through Inspur's California-based subsidiary Aivres via Southeast Asia

confidence.basis: Secondary republication of a New York Times investigation; the primary NYT text was not read directly and the claims are described as allegations, so capped at medium.

dispersion: conflicting same-key reports: magnitude 1 -> 2; sources: freepressjournal.in (New York Times investigation, via IANS)
